To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a reliable energy system based on 100% renewable energies will rely on the following pillars: (1) energy storage, (2) renewable energy overproduction, and (3) smart grids.
the three pillars are: energy storage, overproduction, and smart grids.
the conversion to a 100 %-renewable energy system will require a large-scale deployment of renewable overproduction and energy storage systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sustainable and secure energy supply system for Germany.
the development of a comprehensive energy supply system that is based on renewable energy sources.
the development of a reliable energy supply based on renewable energy sources and their integration in the energy system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the German energy supply system is not yet a 100  % renewable one.
the conversion of today’s global energy system into a 100 % energy system is possible and can be achieved in a short time.
Germany has to rely more and more on energy storage, renewable energy overproduction, and smart grid technology in the future to maintain reliable energy supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the German energy system will have a 100 %-renewable electricity supply in the year 2050.
the German energy system will not be able to rely on the conventional energy mix in the future, but will have to be converted to a system based on renewable energy sources.
we have to change our energy supply systems completely, but we have to keep the same reliability and quality of supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three pillars are not independent but interrelated.
all three pillars have a high potential to increase the renewable energy share in an energy supply system and that they are not mutually exclusive.
all three pillars are needed to achieve a 100  % renewable energy supply and that the pillars are interdependent and mutually supporting.
